extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and applicants for most Research Project Grants (RPGs) (e.g., R01, R21, R03, U01, etc.)
extracted.subtask_description: The Simplified Peer Review Framework describing how reviewers should evaluate most NIH Research Project Grant applications (due Jan 25, 2025 or later), reorganizing the five regulatory criteria into three factors with scoring and guidance for each. Used by reviewers to assign criterion scores and by applicants to understand review expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the three Factors and applicable additional review criteria; an application does not need to be strong in all categories to be judged likely to have major scientific impact. Overall Impact is informed by Factor 1 and Factor 2 scores and Factor 3 adequacy evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1: Importance of the Research (Significance, Innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined factor scored 1–9 that captures Significance and Innovation. Evaluate the importance of the proposed research in the context of current scientific challenges and opportunities and the extent to which innovation influences the importance of undertaking the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance: assess whether the application addresses an important gap, would solve a critical problem, or create a valuable conceptual/technical advance; evaluate rationale, rigor of scientific background (prior literature, preliminary data) and whether background justifies the study. Innovation: evaluate whether the work applies novel concepts, methods or technologies or uses existing approaches in novel ways; note that a project lacking novelty may still be critically important to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2: Rigor and Feasibility (Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined factor scored 1–9 focusing on the Approach, including rigor (likelihood of producing compelling, reproducible findings) and feasibility (whether the studies can be done well and within proposed timeframes). This factor now also incorporates inclusion, clinical trial timelines, and Phase III design/analysis considerations where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigor: evaluate potential to produce unbiased, reproducible, robust data; quality of experimental design and controls; justification of sample size; quality of analysis, interpretation, and reporting plans; plans to address relevant biological variables (e.g., sex, age); for human subjects/animals evaluate rigor of interventions, justification of outcome variables, generalizability or relevance to subgroups, and sample appropriateness/diversity. Feasibility: evaluate whether approach is sound and achievable, including plans to address problems or new challenges; weigh uncertainty against potential for major advances. For human-subject studies and clinical trials evaluate adequacy and feasibility of recruitment/retention plans and likelihood of achieving enrollment; for clinical trials evaluate feasibility of study timeline and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3: Expertise and Resources (Investigators, Environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluated as 'appropriate' or 'gaps identified' (binary assessment; not individually scored). Reviewers must provide an explanation if gaps are identified. Consider Investigator(s) and Environment with respect to the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators: evaluate whether investigators have demonstrated background, training, and expertise appropriate for their career stage to conduct the proposed work; for MPI applications assess the leadership plan to facilitate coordination and collaboration. Environment: evaluate whether institutional resources are appropriate to ensure successful execution of the proposed work. The binary framing is intended to reduce undue influence of general scientific reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications involving non-exempt human subjects or clinical trials, evaluate justification for involvement of human subjects and proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate: (1) risk to subjects; (2) adequacy of protection against risks; (3) potential benefits to subjects and others; (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained; (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For research that meets exempt categories, evaluate justification for exemption, human subjects involvement and characteristics, and sources of materials. See separate Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposed research includes vertebrate animals, evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals according to specific subcriteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate: (1) description of proposed procedures including species, strains, ages, sex, and total number; (2) justification for use of animals versus alternatives and appropriateness of species; (3) interventions to minimize discomfort, distress, pain and injury; (4) justification for euthanasia method if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines. See the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animals Section for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposed research includes biohazards, evaluate potential hazards and proposed protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether materials or procedures are significantly hazardous to personnel and/or the environment and whether adequate protections are proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmissions (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For resubmitted applications, evaluate the full application as now presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether prior reviewer concerns have been addressed and whether the revised application justifies funding in light of prior feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewals (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For renewal (competitive continuation) applications, evaluate progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess accomplishments, productivity, and whether the proposed renewal advances the program/line of research appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For revision applications, evaluate the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the revision is justified, feasible, and how the expanded scope affects the project’s overall merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources (Additional Review Consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: For projects involving key biological and/or chemical resources, reviewers consider plans for identifying and ensuring the validity of those resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the brief plans proposed to authenticate reagents, cell lines, antibodies, etc.; this is a consideration only and does not receive a separate criterion score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support (Additional Review Consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider whether the budget and requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This consideration does not receive a separate score but should inform overall assessment; budget review may be shifted to NIH staff for some items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of Inclusion, Study Timelines, and Phase III Design into Factor 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion criteria/coding, study timelines for clinical trial applications, and plans for valid design and analysis of Phase III clinical trials are now incorporated into Factor 2 (Rigor and Feasibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements should be evaluated as part of the Approach (Factor 2) rather than as separate Additional Review Criteria, emphasizing their importance to scientific merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items Shifted to Administrative Review by NIH Staff (not peer-reviewed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers no longer evaluate certain Additional Review Considerations—these are administratively reviewed by NIH staff prior to funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications from Foreign Organizations, Select Agent research, and Resource Sharing Plans are examples of items shifted away from peer reviewer evaluation and will be handled administratively by NIH staff.
